cards.power: Play this to instantly discard the "Official Narrative" card from play.
cards.lore: Uncle FrizzleBob's epistemic sabotage expansion! No humans, no neutrality, just pure analog financial wrestling!
cards.gradeReason: Deck intro copy, not a role. Tells you what to think, not who to be.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Pulp conspiracy poster. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit tearing a dollar bill in half. Mood: Furious glee.

cards.power: Force your opponent to reveal their hand. Steal all cards with a 'Profit' value.
cards.lore: "It determines how we proceed with our investigation. 9/11 was a crime, and detectives must identify the perpetrators."
cards.gradeReason: You ARE the detective. One sentence, full role, no manual needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Noir detective illustration. Subject: Bloodhound in trenchcoat sniffing a trail of gold coins. Mood: Relentless certainty.

cards.power: Negate any systemic anomaly by declaring it a "random fluke."
cards.lore: "This would be one of the most extraordinary coincidences in the history of mankind if it was a coincidence."
cards.gradeReason: Great lore quote carries it. POWER role is clear once context clicks.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Retro industrial. Subject: Absurd Rube Goldberg machine labeled COINCIDENCE GENERATOR. Mood: Dry bureaucratic menace.

cards.power: Nullify any investigation card.
cards.lore: "You got to go through 10 veils before you get to the real Source, thanks to the Secretary of the Treasury."
cards.gradeReason: Veil-layer role is playable. The abstraction needs one beat of context to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ornate bureaucratic theatre. Subject: Peacock in suit standing behind ten translucent curtains. Mood: Smug obstruction.

cards.power: Control the board's highest value asset for a fraction of the cost.
cards.lore: In 1998, the Port Authority agreed to privatize the WTC. By July 2001, a 99-year lease was signed for $3.2B.
cards.gradeReason: Clear property-grab mechanic. Historical lore makes it land but it's context-dependent.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Corporate propaganda poster. Subject: Frog in hard hat planting a SOLD sign on two giant towers. Mood: Triumphant greed.

cards.power: Leverage 0.4% of your own assets to control a multi-billion dollar empire.
cards.lore: Other players only put down $14 million of their own money, financed by GMAC and individual investors.
cards.gradeReason: 0.4% leverage is immediately playable and outrageous. The ratio alone is the performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Wall Street grotesque. Subject: Fat pig in suit balancing a $3.2B gold bar on a $14 matchstick. Mood: Obscene leverage.

cards.power: Double your coverage right before a disaster. If disaster strikes, claim it happened twice.
cards.lore: The leaseholder insisted on doubling the insurance to $3.55B, demanding courts construe the attacks as two separate events to win $7.1B.
cards.gradeReason: Insurance double-down is pure villain performance. Instantly embodiable, no notes needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Crooked insurance ad. Subject: Squirrel in suit pointing at two identical fire claims. Mood: Cheerful fraud.

cards.power: Get your initial equity refunded while maintaining total control of the site.
cards.lore: In a secret 2003 deal, the Port Authority paid back 80% of the initial equity. Profit: $4.55 billion and counting.
cards.gradeReason: Kickback mechanic is clear. The 2003 timeline requires context to feel like a role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Back-alley deal illustration. Subject: Two reptiles exchanging a briefcase under a streetlight. Mood: Conspiratorial satisfaction.

cards.power: Host the most sensitive data on the exact floors of an impending impact.
cards.lore: Marsh & McLennan occupied the exact impact zone of the North Tower, housing 2,000 employees and critical transaction data.
cards.gradeReason: Strong setup card. Role is the planner who knew — clear but needs the sheet framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Architectural blueprint. Subject: Bear hunched over floor plans with impact zone circled in red. Mood: Cold precision.

cards.power: Execute massive paperless transactions unseen by any other commercial entity on the planet.
cards.lore: Marsh was the first financial company on the planet to employ this specific type of paperless transaction technology.
cards.gradeReason: The invisible transaction role is there, but E-Link as a name is too technical to snap into immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Retro-tech thriller. Subject: Raccoon vanishing behind a waterfall of digital zeros. Mood: Untraceable velocity.

cards.power: Generate phantom purchase orders. If confronted, urge the Feds to look in your own business.
cards.lore: Severe fiscal anomalies and unnecessary hardware sales led investigators to the heart of the Marsh.com mystery.
cards.gradeReason: Phantom purchase orders is a great mechanic. The double-redirect power is clever but takes a beat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Forensic accounting noir. Subject: Fox surrounded by floating receipts stamped VOID. Mood: Gleeful misdirection.

cards.power: Schedule an all-hands meeting in a doomed building, but dial in from home.
cards.lore: The executive who buried the anomaly inquiry was safe at home, while the IT staff investigating the fraud perished in the conference call.
cards.gradeReason: Dial in from home while your auditors die — one sentence, full villain costume, zero assembly required.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dark domestic satire. Subject: Smug bear on couch with phone, skyscrapers burning through window. Mood: Comfortable distance.

cards.power: Retrieve impossible data from ground zero. Refuse to ever speak of it again.
cards.lore: The German firm recovered data showing a massive, unexplained surge in transactions prior to the attacks. Now? "I could not give you any additional information."
cards.gradeReason: Retrieve-and-silence mechanic is clear. The German firm framing needs a moment to locate yourself in it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Spy thriller tech lab. Subject: Crow in lab coat extracting a smoking hard drive from rubble, mouth sealed shut. Mood: Institutional silence.

cards.power: Co-opt mainframe computers externally during a crisis to purge data.
cards.lore: Right before and during the attacks, Deutsche Bank computers were externally taken over for a massive data download and purge.
cards.gradeReason: You are the remote operator. Timing is built in, power is immediate, role is zero-friction.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Hacker thriller. Subject: Shadowy wolf's hands at keyboard, clock showing 40 minutes, data deleting on screen. Mood: Surgical urgency.

cards.power: Mask illicit mega-trades as random market fluctuations.
cards.lore: "It could turn out that Americans went on an absolute shopping binge on that Tuesday morning." — Convar Director, dripping with irony.
cards.gradeReason: The quote is the whole card. POWER is a description, not an invitation to perform anything.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Satirical consumer culture. Subject: Sheep in suits stampeding into a stock exchange labeled MALL. Mood: Willful absurdity.

cards.power: Establish the Official Enemy within 2 hours of an event, deflecting all financial inquiries.
cards.lore: Marsh's Chief of Risk Management wasn't in his doomed office; he was on NBC blaming Bin Laden before the dust settled.
cards.gradeReason: You are the pivot man on live TV. The 2-hour deadline is a ready-to-use dramatic beat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Breaking news grotesque. Subject: Fox in suit at TV anchor desk pointing at a target while buildings burn behind him. Mood: Shameless opportunism.

cards.power: Turn a $180K bet into $2.4 million in a single day.
cards.lore: More than 2,000 contracts betting against United and American Airlines — 30 times the normal volume. "Horrific, evil insider trading."
cards.gradeReason: $180K to $2.4M in a day. The math IS the performance. Instant table energy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Wall Street casino. Subject: Coyote in pinstripe suit raking chips from a crashed airline model. Mood: Audacious avarice.

cards.power: Buy calls on defense contractors right before a 20-year war starts.
cards.lore: A six-fold increase in call options for Raytheon allowed traders to cash in when the military deployed missiles to Afghanistan.
cards.gradeReason: Buy before the war starts. Crystal-clear role, crystal-clear timing. Pure performance card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Military-industrial infomercial. Subject: Eagle in suit holding Raytheon stock ticker next to exploding rocket. Mood: Premeditated profit.

cards.power: Launch global probes that mysteriously fizzle out when they hit US soil.
cards.lore: Foreign finance ministers were certain: "People connected to the terrorists must have been trying to profit from this tragedy."
cards.gradeReason: The investigation-that-stops role is clear. International framing needs one beat of setup.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Spy thriller map room. Subject: Bloodhound following money trail that disappears at US border. Mood: Deliberate incompetence.

cards.power: Destroy all potentially responsive records regarding options trading.
cards.lore: When FOIA researchers asked for the documentary evidence of the pre-9/11 options trading, they were told the records were destroyed.
cards.gradeReason: You ARE the shredder. One noun, total role. FOIA request denied is the ultimate power move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Office horror. Subject: Rat in uniform feeding documents into shredder labeled EVIDENCE. Mood: Bureaucratic obliteration.

cards.power: Double your stock value on airport security systems. Ignore all FBI interviews.
cards.lore: Wirt D. Walker III bought 56,000 shares of Stratex. The FBI never interviewed him because he had "no ties to terrorism."
cards.gradeReason: Stock-and-ignore mechanic is real. The proper name Walker III anchors it to history, not immediate embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Corporate scandal illustration. Subject: Hawk in blazer staring smugly at a soaring stock chart next to airport scanners. Mood: Untouchable privilege.

cards.power: Host the enemy's family for a private equity breakfast on the day of the attack.
cards.lore: The Carlyle Group was meeting in DC with the brother of Osama Bin Laden on the morning of September 11th.
cards.gradeReason: Breakfast with the enemy's brother on that morning — you ARE the host and you know exactly who you are.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Luxury horror. Subject: Vultures in suits at white-tablecloth breakfast, TV showing smoking towers in background. Mood: Untroubled affluence.

cards.power: Route criminal trades through the former firm of the CIA's Executive Director.
cards.lore: The unusual 2,500 contract put order was brokered by the firm formerly chaired by the current #3 man at the CIA.
cards.gradeReason: CIA pipeline role is clear. The former/current distance makes it slightly abstract to inhabit immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Spy noir. Subject: Owl in CIA badge handing a trade slip through a revolving door labeled AB Brown. Mood: Institutional impunity.

cards.power: Possess perfect foresight. Remain uninvestigated forever.
cards.lore: Former CIA agent Robert Baer admitted on video knowing a DOD staffer who cashed out the day before. No agency ever investigated him.
cards.gradeReason: Perfect foresight. Remain uninvestigated forever. Two sentences, two superpowers, zero ambiguity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Beach noir. Subject: Iguana in sunglasses counting cash by the ocean, San Diego skyline behind him. Mood: Prophetic ease.

cards.power: Examine 9.5 million transactions and conclude nothing happened.
cards.lore: They didn't say insider trading didn't happen. They said "those who had advanced knowledge didn't trade." Begging the question: WHO had knowledge?
cards.gradeReason: The circular-logic regulator role is great. The LORE analysis is editorial, not pure performance fuel.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Official absurdism. Subject: Blind horse in SEC uniform stamping CLEARED on a mountain of documents. Mood: Procedural blindness.

cards.power: Place 95% of the put options on an airline and get a free pass.
cards.lore: The 9/11 Commission dismissed the trades because the US-based investor had "no conceivable ties to Al-Qaeda."
cards.gradeReason: 95% concentration is a wild fact. Get a free pass needs the Commission logic to snap into place.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Commission hearing grotesque. Subject: Pig at witness stand shrugging while 95% bar chart floats behind it. Mood: Teflon confidence.

cards.power: Prove beyond a statistical doubt that insiders traded. Get completely ignored by the government.
cards.lore: Three separate scientific papers concluded with high probability that the anomalous trading was the result of advanced knowledge.
cards.gradeReason: Prove-and-be-ignored is a clean tragicomic arc. Needs the academic identity to inhabit fully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Academic tragedy. Subject: Owl professor presenting statistical graphs to completely empty government hearing chairs. Mood: Righteous futility.

cards.power: Declare the origin of the money "of little practical significance."
cards.lore: The final word of the US Government rejected the first rule of criminal investigation: Follow the Money.
cards.gradeReason: Bureaucratic dismissal role is clear. The card leans on lore irony to land — power alone is thin.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Official ceremony satire. Subject: Pelican in suit waving away a mountain of dollar bills with one flip of the wing. Mood: Authoritative indifference.

cards.power: Map and monitor a target's entire system and personnel in real time.
cards.lore: The ultimate risk management software. The person running it has a God's eye view to foresee problems—or cause them.
cards.gradeReason: God's eye view — you are the all-seeing architect. Immediate, total, thrilling role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Surveillance tech horror. Subject: Giant eye inside a web of government building blueprints. Mood: Omniscient calm.

cards.power: Merge risk management and enterprise architecture to prevent—or execute—massive failures.
cards.lore: JP Morgan sought software to stop rogue trading and massive computer failures. Ptech was the industry guru recommendation.
cards.gradeReason: Prevent-or-execute duality is sharp. The JP Morgan context anchors it — needs that beat to work at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Corporate thriller diagram. Subject: Gecko in boardroom unveiling blueprints labeled both SHIELD and SWORD. Mood: Dual-use menace.

cards.cardName: The Keys to the Cyber Kingdom
cards.power: Gain top-level security clearance to the most protected servers in the world.
cards.lore: Ptech built detailed pictures of agency vulnerabilities, showing exactly how they could be exploited by those of ill intent.
cards.gradeReason: You hold ALL the keys. Maximal access, zero friction to inhabit. Pure G1 power move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Heist thriller. Subject: Wolf in developer hoodie holding a giant keyring with IRS, FBI, NATO, White House labels. Mood: Quiet omnipotence.

cards.power: Find the exact holes in the defense escalation process.
cards.lore: Ptech worked in the FAA basement, specifically looking for holes in how agencies respond to a hijacking emergency.
cards.gradeReason: Role is real but interoperability is a jargon speed bump. Table needs the Ptech sheet context first.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Technical thriller. Subject: Raccoons in FAA basement mapping hijacking response gaps on a whiteboard. Mood: Methodical infiltration.

cards.power: Seize $1.4M in terror funds, then get permanently blocked by your own bosses.
cards.lore: Agents Wright and Vincent were thwarted from opening a criminal investigation into the very man financing Ptech.
cards.gradeReason: The blocked-agent role is emotionally clear. Vulgar Betrayal title is strong but the mechanic needs setup.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Institutional tragedy. Subject: Two bloodhounds straining at leashes held by their own police chief. Mood: Institutional sabotage.

cards.power: Boast of ties to the Vice President while funding startups and terror simultaneously.
cards.lore: The multi-millionaire angel investor behind Ptech was later put on a US Treasury terrorist watch list.
cards.gradeReason: Named character = instant costume. VP ties plus terror funding simultaneously — the split identity is the performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Society portrait gone wrong. Subject: Leopard in tux shaking hands with VP while signing terror check behind his back. Mood: Brazen duality.

cards.power: Provide $5 million in seed capital to infiltrate the US government.
cards.lore: The investment firm backed by al-Qadi that got Ptech off the ground.
cards.gradeReason: Infiltration-via-investment is clear. The entity name is opaque without the al-Qadi context from card 34.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Corporate cover art. Subject: Scorpion signing a venture capital check labeled PTECH in a glass-walled boardroom. Mood: Laundered legitimacy.

cards.power: Create a financial facade to conceal terror support.
cards.lore: Shared office space with al-Qadi, provided founding loans for Ptech, and was run by Ptech's own Chief Scientist.
cards.gradeReason: Multi-function shell company role is there but requires three facts to assemble. Dense for table play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Shell company diagram. Subject: Horse in hardhat holding For Lease sign over a building with three secret doors. Mood: Layered concealment.

cards.power: Write software for the government by day, praise holy war by night.
cards.lore: Ptech's Chief Architect quoted Bin Laden's mentor while mapping the operational blueprints of the US military.
cards.gradeReason: Government coder by day, radical by night — dual identity is immediately playable with zero setup.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Split-screen identity portrait. Subject: Wolf at computer coding, half in government badge half in shadow. Mood: Double life as daily routine.

cards.power: Delay a federal raid by two weeks to ensure all evidence is gone.
cards.lore: When the FBI finally raided Ptech in 2002, the company was given two weeks advanced warning.
cards.gradeReason: You are whoever tipped them off. Two weeks advance warning is a story you can tell in one breath.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Spy comedy. Subject: Turtle mailman delivering RAID SCHEDULED letter to office with two-week countdown calendar. Mood: Absurd complicity.

cards.power: Declare an infiltrated system perfectly safe the day after a raid.
cards.lore: Ridge declared that Ptech "in no way jeopardizes the security of the country."
cards.gradeReason: Rubber stamp the day after is sharp irony. Named character helps but the timing is the whole joke.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Bureaucratic satire. Subject: Bulldog in Homeland Security uniform stamping FINE on a smoking server rack. Mood: Institutional damage control.

cards.power: Co-chair an investigation while ignoring your own financial ties.
cards.lore: Kean had a $24M real estate transaction with BMI. The Commission never looked into Ptech.
cards.gradeReason: Conflict-of-interest investigator is a great role. The $24M BMI connection needs prior cards to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Official portrait corruption. Subject: Swan in suit chairing hearing while stuffing BMI paperwork into briefcase. Mood: Genteel self-dealing.

cards.power: Declare war on your own bureaucracy 24 hours before a catastrophe.
cards.lore: "The adversary is closer to home... It's the Pentagon bureaucracy."
cards.gradeReason: Rumsfeld naming the Pentagon as the enemy on 9/10 — the timing makes you perform it before you finish reading.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Martial press conference. Subject: Eagle at podium pointing accusingly at Pentagon building, calendar shows Sept 10. Mood: Preemptive misdirection.

cards.power: Fudge entries, process without documentation, or make them up entirely.
cards.lore: In 1999 alone, $2.3 trillion in transactions could not be properly accounted for, $8,000 for every citizen in America.
cards.gradeReason: Fudge-the-books role is clear. The trillion-dollar scale is staggering but the role itself is procedural.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Pentagon accounting horror. Subject: Bear pushing stacks of cash under a rug labeled RECONCILED. Mood: Industrial-scale nonchalance.

cards.power: Reassign anyone who cares about doing a good job.
cards.lore: Jim Minnery tried to track down $300 million. His director asked him, "Why do you care about this stuff?"
cards.gradeReason: You ARE the director asking why do you care. Weaponized indifference as a power — perfect ironic performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Office satire. Subject: Manager shrugging at accountant holding $300M receipt, reassignment form already in hand. Mood: Institutional apathy as policy.

cards.power: Fail to untangle the financial snarl, but get a massive defense budget anyway.
cards.lore: Tasked with solving the $2.3 trillion missing money, Zakheim instead drafted papers calling for military transformation.
cards.gradeReason: Fail-upward role is classic. The Zakheim-to-PNAC pipeline needs one beat of context to fully reward.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Bureaucratic ladder climbing. Subject: Octopus with ledger full of question marks signing Pentagon budget increase. Mood: Failing upward at scale.

cards.power: Develop remote control systems for airborne vehicles, then market them to the Pentagon.
cards.lore: Zakheim's former company provided advanced military electronics and remote flight tech to DARPA prior to 9/11.
cards.gradeReason: Remote flight tech for DARPA is a loaded factual card. Role needs the Zakheim sheet framing to click.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Cold war tech thriller. Subject: Owl engineer holding remote control with paper plane labeled DARPA looping in background. Mood: Plausible deniability.

cards.power: Write a white paper predicting exactly what you need to conquer the world.
cards.lore: PNAC called for a sweeping transformation of the military, including biological warfare targeting specific genotypes.
cards.gradeReason: White-paper-as-blueprint role is sharp. The biological genotype detail is the wildest fact and slightly buries the lede.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Think tank thriller. Subject: Lions in suits presenting a world map with color-coded invasion zones. Mood: Academic menace.

cards.power: Receive a catastrophic and catalyzing event exactly when your political agenda requires it.
cards.lore: "The process of transformation... is likely to be a long one, absent some catastrophic and catalyzing event."
cards.gradeReason: PNAC quote plus exactly when your political agenda requires it — you step into the author's shoes the moment you read it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Document thriller. Subject: Hand circling catastrophic and catalyzing event in a classified document. Calendar shows Sept 2001. Mood: Prophetic planning.

cards.power: Use a crisis to bypass all political opposition to a $50 billion budget increase.
cards.lore: "We know that the thing that tends to register on people is fear... we've got to be smarter than that."
cards.gradeReason: Fear as budget instrument — you are the fear manager. The $50B result seals the performance in one move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Political horror campaign. Subject: Deer-in-headlights citizens herded toward a $50B budget approval stamp. Mood: Engineered panic.

cards.power: Concentrate your entire financial auditing team in a single, newly renovated target zone.
cards.lore: The office of Resource Services Washington had just moved back into Wedge 1. 34 bookkeepers and budget analysts were killed.
cards.gradeReason: Planner-who-concentrated-the-auditors role is chilling. Needs the Pentagon trillions context to feel like a performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Floor plan horror. Subject: Blueprint of Pentagon Wedge 1 with all accounting offices circled in red. Mood: Architectural precision meets tragedy.

cards.power: Lose the personnel required to ever figure out where the missing trillions went.
cards.lore: The Army was unable to produce a financial report for 2001 due to the loss of accountants in the attack.
cards.gradeReason: Auditors gone, books unbalanceable — clean dark mechanic. But it's passive: something happened TO the audit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Government tragedy. Subject: Empty accountant desks with unfinished balance sheets, Pentagon smoke outside window. Mood: Permanent incompleteness.

cards.power: Hire the masterminds of corporate accounting fraud to run the military's budget.
cards.lore: Before becoming Secretary of the Army, White was a senior executive at Enron, the largest accounting fraud in history.
cards.gradeReason: You ARE the Enron man at the Army's helm. Career-as-credential-for-fraud is immediately wearable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Rogues gallery portrait. Subject: Fox in Army uniform with Enron logo pin on lapel, reviewing Pentagon ledgers. Mood: Revolving door confidence.

cards.power: Destroy 3,000 to 4,000 documents on active corporate fraud investigations.
cards.lore: The SEC occupied floors 11-13 of WTC Building 7, wiping out evidence on Enron and others when it collapsed.
cards.gradeReason: You are the building. 3,000-4,000 documents — you don't need to explain what happened, the math speaks.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Evidence room noir. Subject: Filing cabinets labeled ENRON INVESTIGATION tumbling into rubble, Building 7 collapsing behind. Mood: Convenient catastrophe.

cards.power: Inflate the unaccountable money from $2.3T to $8.5T over a decade without a single Congressional hearing.
cards.lore: Rumsfeld's war on the Pentagon bureaucracy was highly successful at losing even more money.
cards.gradeReason: Scale escalation is staggering. But inflate without a hearing is a situation, not a character to wear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Congressional absurdism. Subject: Bear rolling a snowball labeled $2.3T down a hill, it becomes $8.5T at the bottom. Mood: Effortless scale.

cards.power: Doctor books to hide missing money using standard operating procedure.
cards.lore: If money is missing at the end of the day, just input a false number to cover it up and submit a balanced budget.
cards.gradeReason: Just input a false number is a great line but the role is the accountant, not a character with bite.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Office procedural horror. Subject: Mouse at Pentagon terminal changing $2.3T to $0.00, boss approving with a stamp. Mood: Bureaucratic corruption as routine.

cards.power: Spend 15 years falsifying financial records for the Navy.
cards.lore: "Money was missing from the report every month."
cards.gradeReason: 15-year forgery career is wild. But the card tells her story rather than handing you her costume.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Long-con portrait. Subject: Raccoon at desk surrounded by 15 years of Navy ledgers, eraser worn to a nub. Mood: Exhausted complicity.

cards.power: Completely lose $6 billion in cash in a war zone.
cards.lore: The US wasted $50 billion and completely lost $6 billion in Iraq. That's more than most countries spend on their entire defense in a year.
cards.gradeReason: Completely lose $6 billion in cash is peak absurdism. But losing money is passive — the loser-as-role needs more.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Desert war comedy. Subject: Camel standing next to a crater labeled $6B shrugging at a US general. Mood: Weaponized incompetence.

cards.power: Combine Insurance, Insider Trading, and Military Fraud to win the pot.
cards.lore: Insurance scams, financial fraud, missing money, and evidence destroyed. $8.5 trillion remains to investigate.
cards.gradeReason: You are the final boss who ran all three scams simultaneously. Full roster, full accountability, full performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Final boss splash art. Subject: Three-headed lizard in suit holding insurance policy, stock ticker, and Pentagon budget. Mood: Total systemic control.

cards.power: Ask the perpetrators to investigate themselves.
cards.lore: The answers to 9/11 are not going to come from the suspects of the crime.
cards.gradeReason: You ARE the perpetrator writing the investigation. Self-investigation as power move — one sentence, whole costume.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Commission theatre. Subject: Fox presiding over hearing table with all other seats also filled by foxes. Mood: Closed-loop justice.

cards.power: Ensure that potentially responsive records are always "destroyed."
cards.lore: From CBOE to Convar, the evidence of the money trail always manages to disappear into the ether.
cards.gradeReason: Records-always-disappear is a clean systemic card. The passive always manages to disappear is irony, not a role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Evidence trail vanishing act. Subject: Paper trail from CBOE to Convar, each document bursting into smoke. Mood: Systemic erasure.

cards.power: Discard all illusions. Game over.
cards.lore: "They told you 9/11 changed everything. They were right: it made the house infinitely rich. Follow the Kayfabe-Money, kids!"
cards.gradeReason: FrizzleBob in the room. Full character, full verdict, maximum table energy. The deck ends where it should.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Final panel splash. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit MC standing on a pile of gold coins, pointing at the camera. Mood: Vindicated fury.

verdict: The Kayfabe Money Trail 9/11 deck hits like a dossier landing on your breakfast table — dense, documented, and furious about it. Named strength: the Insider Trading Casino and Ptech Cyber Kingdom sheets are G1 gold, every card a ready-to-wear villain costume. Named weakness: Sheet 13 ($8.5 Trillion Couch Change) is four consecutive procedural G2s that slow table energy right before the finale. Table-ready: Yes.
blurb: For truth-seekers and table fighters who know the official narrative is missing a decimal point. 60 cards of documented financial forensics across 14 sheets — cut, shuffle, and follow the kayfabe-money.

coverQA.coverVisual: 4 — Four-panel KKKK intro grid, full illustrated cards, consistent FrizzleBob art style throughout.
coverQA.coverTitle: 4 — 9/11 Trillions: Follow The Kayfabe-Money! with EXPANDS! header lands the brand and the angle cleanly.
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Dark financial conspiracy meets absurdist rabbit universe — perfect vibe coherence.
coverQA.coverOriginality: 3 — Standard KKKK add-on cover format, no structural innovation over other series decks.
coverQA.coverViral: 4 — 9/11 plus Kayfabizarro plus scissors instruction is provocative and shareable.
coverQA.coverNote: The cover does exactly what a KKKK expansion needs: flash the four anchor cards, establish the rabbit hole, hand the player a reason to cut. The EXPANDS! header is doing heavy lifting — without it you'd need three sentences of context. Four stars, no notes, just don't lose the exclamation mark.

notes: ADD-ON deck (14 numbered content sheets + 1 cover/intro sheet = 15 pages total). 2x2 card grid per page, cut-and-play KKKK format. Card 1 (9/11 Trillions) functions as an intro/rules card embedded in the cover — structurally a card but texturally a deck preamble. KayfaBINGO! and Follow Fluffy! speech bubbles appear on several cards as recurring FrizzleBob design elements. All fonts are intentional design choices (Bangers headers, decorative body text). No RAF dice boxes present. Sheet 13 ($8.5 Trillion) has the weakest card density — four G2 procedural cards with no G1 anchor. Sheet 14 (FrizzleBob's Final Suplex) recovers strongly with 3 G1 cards including the verdict card.

urgent: Upgrade card 1 (9/11 Trillions) — currently pure deck copy, not a playable card; rewrite as a performative mechanic or relabel as intro card
quickWins: Give Sheet 13 ($8.5 Trillion Couch Change) one G1 anchor card — Linda Woodford's Eraser is closest, sharpen POWER to be a role not a description
Card 15 (The Absolute Shopping Binge) POWER needs a character to inhabit — the Convar Director quote is great but mask trades as fluctuations is passive description
niceToHave: Add a Series ID badge on each sheet header for bundle coherence
Consider splitting Ptech sheets (7-9) into a standalone Ptech mini-deck — content is strong enough to stand alone

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: THE KAYFABE MONEY TRAIL (9/11) – Follow the Receipts, Not the Smoke (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

A good magician keeps your eyes on the smoke. The expensive part of the trick always happens at the cashier's window.

On the afternoon of September 10, 2001, the Secretary of Defense stepped up to a podium and admitted out loud that the Pentagon could not account for 2.3 trillion dollars. For a few hours it was the biggest number in the country. By the following evening nobody wanted to discuss the ledger again for twenty years, and the largest missing sum in modern bookkeeping quietly became the one figure polite people agreed to leave alone. This deck picks that thread back up exactly where everyone was told to drop it.

The Kayfabe Money Trail is documented financial forensics you can shuffle. Sixty cut-and-play cards rebuild the paper trail on your kitchen table, and you argue each transaction out loud with a straight face while the room decides whether the official version survives contact with the bank statement. This is Social Story Wrestling for the accountant's side of the story, the side that does not photograph well and never makes the anniversary montage.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Money Trail Core Deck: 60 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring The Double-Trouble Policy, Rumsfeld's Declaration, and Paul Bremer's NBC Pivot.
- The Freestyle Rules: The complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math beyond the math that already went missing, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the one law that every card can claim anything, as long as you can sell the receipt before someone slaps down KayfaBINGO.
- The Fourteen-Sheet Audit: the deck runs the money from the insurance windfall through the reconstruction contracts and the no-bid awards to the careers that walked out of the smoke with a promotion, fourteen numbered sheets you fan into one long trail and read end to end.
